title: Commercial Space Federation (CSF) Welcomes Two New Associate Members
summary: The Commercial Space Federation (CSF) announced the addition of Outlier and Rendezvous Robotics as new Associate Members, highlighting their expertise in reusable satellite platforms and adaptable technologies.

title: Speed to Field Starts Below the Prime
summary: The article discusses the defense industrial base from various perspectives, including a warfighter's viewpoint and insights from major defense companies. It emphasizes the importance of speed in fielding new technologies.

title: The electronics ‘under the hood’ of space networking
summary: SpaceNews interviews Jeff Janicik, founder and chairman of Innoflight, about space networking electronics, Golden Dome, Artemis, and collaborations with the Space Development Agency.

title: LatConnect 60 and Phi Earth Partner to Connect Space and Soil
summary: LatConnect 60 and Phi Earth have partnered to integrate satellite data with ground-based environmental observations for nature-based projects. This collaboration aims to enhance the accuracy and utility of environmental monitoring.

title: RTX’s Blue Canyon Technologies introduces new spacecraft mission enabler
summary: Blue Canyon Technologies, a part of RTX's Raytheon business, has introduced a new spacecraft subsystem to enhance mission capabilities for small satellites. This innovation aims to support the growing demands of the space industry.

title: The threat environment and processing at the edge
summary: SpaceNews interviews FrontGrade CTO Lorne Graves about how spacecraft processing power is adapting to megaconstellations and the benefits of satellite edge processing.

title: Propulsion is having a moment
summary: Space propulsion technology is gaining significant attention in the space industry. Kevin Lausten, CEO of Morpheus Space, discusses its critical importance at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference.

title: Space Angel secures $1.75m WA Government backing to advance Western Australian spaceport plans
summary: Space Angel received a $1.75 million grant from the Western Australian Government to advance plans for a spaceport. The funding was announced by Science and Innovation Minister Stephen Dawson.

title: Tendeg Launches NewTEN Steerable Compact Antenna at SmallSat
summary: Tendeg unveiled NewTEN, a two-axis steerable reflector antenna designed to enhance communications performance and pointing access for small spacecraft. The product was introduced at the SmallSat event in Salt Lake City.

title: Robotics and the future of on-orbit labor
summary: SpaceNews interviews Icarus Robotics CEO Ethan Barajas at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference about the role of robotics in future on-orbit labor. The discussion highlights advancements in autonomous systems for space operations.

title: 5 planets will light up the September sky — here's how to see them
summary: Five planets—Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn—will be visible in the September sky. Stargazers can observe them at specific times and locations.

title: Repairing the ISS 250 miles above Earth | Space photo of the day for Sept. 1, 2026
summary: ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot is shown repairing the International Space Station (ISS) from 250 miles above Earth in a photo taken on Sept. 1, 2026. The image highlights the staggering altitude of the crewed laboratory in orbit.

title: Watch 2 astronauts take 6th-ever all-female spacewalk today
summary: NASA astronaut Jessica Meir and France's Sophie Adenot will conduct the sixth all-female spacewalk outside the International Space Station today (Sept. 1), and you can watch it live.

title: NASA's doomed Swift space telescope restarts science work after rescue mission fails
summary: NASA's Swift space telescope has resumed science observations after a private mission failed to boost its decaying orbit. The telescope is now making the most of its remaining time in space.

title: 'No guts, no glory': How I captured NASA's Roman Space Telescope cross the sun on a picture-perfect SpaceX Falcon Heavy launch
summary: A Space.com photographer captured NASA's Roman Space Telescope crossing the sun during a SpaceX Falcon Heavy launch. The shot was taken from a Hobby Lobby parking lot.

title: What's next for Roman Space Telescope? Here's how NASA's flagship observatory will open up the universe
summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has launched but will take time before starting its science mission. The next steps for the observatory are outlined.

summary: SpaceX and NASA have delayed the Crew-13 mission to the ISS due to an oxidizer leak on the Dragon spacecraft. A new launch date has not been set.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 31, 1965: NASA's ginormous Super Guppy carrier plane takes 1st flight like a flying whale
summary: NASA's Super Guppy cargo plane, known for its distinctive 'flying whale' shape, conducted its first test flight on August 31, 1965. This aircraft played a crucial role in transporting oversized components for the Apollo program.

title: Roman telescope leaves its rocket behind | Space photo of the day for Aug. 31, 2026
summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope was captured deploying into space shortly after launch. The image marks a significant milestone for the next-generation telescope.

title: APOD: 2026 September 1 – A Plane Lunar Eclipse
summary: The Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) for September 1, 2026, features an image of a plane lunar eclipse. The event is highlighted as a fascinating celestial occurrence.

summary: NASA welcomed Türkiye as the 71st signatory of the Artemis Accords during a ceremony hosted by NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. This marks Türkiye's commitment to peaceful and transparent space exploration alongside an international coalition.

title: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope Launches
summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket from Kennedy Space Center in Florida on August 30, 2026. The telescope, named after NASA's first chief astronomer, will survey billions of stars and galaxies with a field of view far larger than Hubble's.

summary: NASA's Roman Space Telescope is on a three-month journey to the Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 2 (L2) and is undergoing commissioning to prepare for science operations.

title: APOD: 2026 August 31 – Launch of the Roman Space Telescope
summary: NASA's Roman Space Telescope is scheduled for launch on August 31, 2026. The mission aims to advance astronomical research and deepen our understanding of the universe.

title: Ribbon-Cutting Event for NASA Deep Space Network’s Deep Space Station 23
summary: NASA held a ribbon-cutting event for the newly completed Deep Space Station 23 antenna at the Goldstone Deep Space Network complex. The event was attended by leadership from NASA Headquarters, Jet Propulsion Laboratory, and the Deep Space Network.

summary: NASA's Deep Space Network completed the new Deep Space Station 23, a 34-meter multifrequency beam-waveguide antenna at the Goldstone complex in California. The antenna will significantly enhance NASA's deep space communications capabilities for decades.

title: Panorama Showcasing the 34-Meter Antennas of the DSN’s Goldstone Complex
summary: A panorama showcases five 34-meter antennas at the Deep Space Network's Goldstone complex in California, including the recently completed Deep Space Station 23. The image highlights the antennas soaking in the summer sun in August 2026.

title: Launch Preview: Array of international launches planned this week
summary: Six international space missions are scheduled to launch this week from various global launch sites. The launches span multiple countries and organizations.

title: SLS picks up the pace, four vehicles in production
summary: NASA and its contractors are accelerating production of the Space Launch System (SLS), with four vehicles currently in development ahead of the Artemis III mission planned for next year. The progress marks a significant step toward the agency's lunar exploration goals.

title: NASA, SpaceX successfully launch the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope from Florida
summary: NASA and SpaceX successfully launched the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope from Florida. This mission marks a significant milestone for space observatories.

title: ESA awards first European Launcher Challenge contracts
summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) has awarded the first contracts under its European Launcher Challenge. This initiative aims to foster innovation and competition in Europe's launch services sector.

title: Soyuz MS-28 departs the ISS, three spacewalks install upgrades to solar arrays and antennae
summary: The Soyuz MS-28 spacecraft departed from the International Space Station. Three spacewalks were conducted to install upgrades to solar arrays and antennae.

summary: SpaceX has announced plans for 'Starbase, Louisiana,' which is set to become the largest private spaceport in the world. The facility will expand SpaceX's launch capabilities and support future missions.

title: Starbase’s future production capacity ramping up
summary: Starbase's production capacity is increasing due to heightened activity at the site. This expansion is likely aimed at supporting future spaceflight missions.

summary: This week will feature five orbital launches, including SpaceX's Falcon Heavy launching the Roman Space Telescope and a Falcon 9 deploying Starlink satellites. The launches will take place from China, the United States, and French Guiana.

title: NASA’s Roman telescope nears launch, reaches final integration and rehearsal milestones
summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is nearing its launch, scheduled for August 30, after completing final integration and rehearsal milestones.

title: LandSpace’s Zhuque-3 topples following milestone landing
summary: LandSpace's Zhuque-3 rocket toppled after achieving a significant milestone with its first stage landing. This marks a critical step for China's commercial space industry.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates 50 years with a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements. The publication marks five decades of the European Space Agency's contributions to space exploration.

title: Phoenix 3: concept study for a reusable European spacecraft
summary: Engineers from ESA and industry partners completed a concept study for Phoenix 3, a reusable spacecraft for microgravity experiments and Earth return.

title: Proba-3’s eclipse hours before totality in Europe
summary: Proba-3 mission will create an artificial solar eclipse to study the Sun's corona before the total solar eclipse in Europe. The mission is designed to observe the Sun's outer atmosphere with high precision.

title: A double eclipse for Proba-3
summary: Proba-3 will experience a double eclipse as the Moon crosses its field of view. This event is part of its mission operations.

title: How ESA mimics and models the 2026 total solar eclipse
summary: ESA is preparing to study the 2026 total solar eclipse by using artificial eclipse missions and computer simulations to observe the Sun's corona, which is otherwise difficult to study due to the rarity and brief duration of natural eclipses.

summary: The European Space Agency is inviting European researchers and companies to run their software aboard the Hera mission, which will travel millions of kilometers into deep space. This is a unique opportunity for testing software in a real deep-space environment.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESTEC, the European Space Agency's technical centre in the Netherlands.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will use a coronagraph to study the Sun's corona by blocking the Sun's disk, creating an artificial eclipse. The mission involves two satellites working in tandem to achieve this.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event on 16–17 September at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands will bring together startup companies and the European space industry to exchange ideas, showcase capabilities, and explore collaborations.

title: Exclusive: Helogen Plans Two In-Orbit Manufacturing Missions in October
summary: Helogen is planning two in-orbit manufacturing missions in October, marking the first flights of its HEL-IOS platform. The company has previously flown subsystems but has not yet launched the full platform.

title: Diffraqtion Adds to Pre-Seed Round for Quantum Camera Tech
summary: Diffraqtion secured additional funding for its quantum camera technology, bringing its total pre-seed round to over $10M with investments from Lockheed Martin Ventures and Sumitomo Corporation’s Presidio Ventures.

title: Roman Space Telescope Begins Its Journey to L2

summary: Canadian companies are collaborating on a Space Development Agency (SDA) satellite solution, while SpaceX and LeoLabs expand their space domain awareness (SDA) capabilities with new initiatives.

title: LeoLabs Wins $20.68M Space Force Award for Scout
summary: LeoLabs secured a $20.68 million contract with the U.S. Space Force to deploy its radar technology for national security missions. The award was announced on Wednesday.

summary: All.Space has secured a contract from the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) to boost production rates for its Hydra satcom terminal under a U.S. defense supply chain initiative.

summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) has selected NorthStar Earth & Space to lead a study on uncontrolled atmospheric re-entry. NorthStar’s European subsidiary will head a consortium for ESA’s Forecasting of Uncontrolled Reentry initiative.

summary: OHB secured a nearly €1 billion contract to build 18 Medium-Earth Orbit (MEO) satellites for Europe's IRIS² constellation. The deal was awarded by SES, as announced on Monday.

title: India’s InspeCity Raises $10.5M in Pre-Series A round

title: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Telescope Launches on Falcon Heavy Rocket
summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Telescope launched on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket. The mission marks a significant step in space-based astronomy.

summary: Europe's Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) constellation is now complete after Arianespace launched the second imaging satellite on Aug. 27. The European meteorological agency EUMETSAT confirmed the successful deployment of MTG-I2.

title: Ovzon to Enter German Market With New Partnerships
summary: Swedish satellite operator Ovzon is entering the German market through two new partnerships, including an initial test implementation with a German government entity.

title: PLD Space, Isar Aerospace, and Rocket Factory Augsburg Land ESA Contracts in Launch Challenge
summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) awarded over 500 million euros to PLD Space, Isar Aerospace, and Rocket Factory Augsburg as part of the European Launch Challenge. This funding supports the development of new launch capabilities within Europe.
